mem.t: Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.

lessons.title: Jesus, Gentle and Humble in Heart
lessons.theme: Gentleness is not weakness; it is having power and refusing to use it to crush others

v: “Come to me, all you who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart; and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.”

lessons.still: Relax your shoulders and notice the burdens you are carrying: work, family, relationships, worries. Breathe out slowly and picture yourself setting them down and taking up the Lord’s easy yoke instead. Softly say, “Lord, I come to learn from you.”
teach: A horse that has been broken in has lost none of its strength; it simply no longer charges about wildly, but responds to its master’s reins. In biblical times, Greek often used the word for “gentleness” to describe this kind of tamed strength. Gentleness is not a lack of strength; it is strength placed in God’s hands.

When Jesus described himself, he did not say, “I am mighty in heart,” but “I am gentle and humble in heart.” A yoke is carried by two oxen together, and Jesus invites us to share his yoke — he walks beside us, bears the weight, and sets our pace. To learn from him is to learn his gentle and humble heart.

This week we are learning the fruit of gentleness. Gentleness is not a naturally easygoing temperament. It belongs to a person who has accepted their place before God and so has no need to protect themselves by being hard. A change of mindset: gentleness is not losing; it is a strength only a heart at rest can have.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Jesus is my example. Humility is laying down power and returning to our place; gentleness is what humility looks like in our relationships. Self-ruled people use their strength to control others; people living the self-emptied life hand their strength to God, so they can treat others gently and find rest for their own souls.
q: Who is God? — The almighty Lord says, “I am gentle and humble in heart” — what does that show you about God?
Who am I? — Do you use your “strength” (your words, position, or knowledge) to push people down or to lift them up?
How shall I respond? — In which relationship will you learn from Jesus today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus rode into Jerusalem on a donkey’s colt — a king who came not on a warhorse but on a colt. He had authority to calm storms and drive out unclean spirits, yet he took little children in his arms and touched lepers; a bruised reed he would not break. His gentleness is the gentleness of the Almighty.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, gentle and humble, I lay down my burdens and come to you. I am willing to take your yoke and learn from you. Tame the hasty, hard self within me, and keep all my strength in your hands, to be used for lifting people up and never for pressing them down. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: When you speak today, deliberately slow down and lower your voice
With one of “my 2,” use a gentle tone in place of your usual hurrying or ordering
lessons.noon: “Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart.” — Lord, right now I learn from you.

lessons.title: Moses, the Humblest of Men
lessons.theme: Those whom God affirms need not rush to defend themselves

v: They said, “Has the LORD indeed spoken only with Moses? Hasn’t he spoken also with us?” And the LORD heard it.
Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the men who were on the surface of the earth.
My servant Moses is not so. He is faithful in all my house.

lessons.still: Remember a time you were misunderstood or criticised. Don’t hurry to defend yourself in your mind; quietly hand it over to the Lord: “Lord, you heard it all.” Let God be your defender; all you need to do is return to him.
teach: A deeply rooted tree doesn’t topple when someone kicks it, nor is it in a hurry to kick back. Miriam and Aaron — Moses’ own sister and brother — publicly challenged his authority. Attacked by those closest to him, Moses did not hit back. Scripture simply inserts one sentence at this point: “Now the man Moses was very humble, above all the men who were on the surface of the earth.”

“And Yahweh heard it.” Moses did not need to defend himself, because God himself stepped in and said, “My servant Moses… is faithful in all my house.” Humility is not having no convictions; it is entrusting your reputation to God. Later, when Miriam was punished, it was Moses who cried out to God to heal her — a gentle person can even intercede for the one who hurt him.

As a young man, Moses killed an Egyptian in a fit of passion — that was self-ruled strength. After forty years in the wilderness, he became “very humble.” Gentleness is refined in us by God. A change of mindset: when I am criticised, I don’t have to rush to prove I am right, because my worth was settled long ago in God.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Let people be people and let God be God. Self-ruled people insist on vindicating themselves and guarding their own reputation; people living the self-emptied life return to their place and let God be God. Pride provokes pride: had Moses hit back, the family would have been torn apart. He chose humility, and God himself vindicated him.
q: Who is God? — “And Yahweh heard it” — how have you experienced God as your defender?
Who am I? — When you are misunderstood, is your first reaction to defend yourself, to hit back, or to entrust it to God?
How shall I respond? — What part of your “reputation” do you need to hand over to God’s protection today?
lessons.jesus: When Jesus was falsely accused before Pilate, he “gave him no answer, not even one word, so that the governor marveled greatly.” It was not that he had nothing to say; he entrusted himself to the Father, who judges justly. His silence was not weakness but the deepest gentleness and trust.
lessons.pray: Lord, I confess that when I am misunderstood I am quick to defend myself, and even to strike back. Refine me as you refined Moses, and make me a humble person. I hand my reputation over to you; you are my defender. Help me to pray for those who hurt me. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: When you are criticised today, pause for three seconds and pray silently before you respond
Pray for someone who once misunderstood you
When you disagree with one of “my 2,” listen all the way through before rushing to explain yourself
lessons.noon: “Now the man Moses was very humble, more than all the men who were on the surface of the earth.” — Lord, right now I leave my defence to you.

lessons.title: The Gentle Shall Inherit the Earth
lessons.theme: Those who do not grab and fight end up receiving God’s inheritance

v: Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.
But the humble shall inherit the land, and shall delight themselves in the abundance of peace.

lessons.still: Think of something you have badly wanted to win lately, or are afraid to lose: a position, some recognition, an opportunity. Slowly open your clenched hand, hold it out before the Lord, and say, “Lord, my inheritance is in your hands.”
teach: The world’s logic says that if you want land, you must be tough — you must fight and grab. Throughout history, land has mostly been won by the sword. Yet Jesus said something that turns this upside down: “Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.” To “inherit” means to receive as heirs — the inheritance is not seized; it is given by the Father.

Jesus’ words echo Psalm 37. Seeing the wicked prosper, the psalmist urges, “Don’t fret,” but rest quietly and trust in the Lord. The gentle are not blind to injustice; they believe God governs all things, so they don’t need to grab with their own hands. God himself will give the inheritance to his children.

Self-ruled people are afraid of losing out, so they fight; people living the self-emptied life know they are God’s children, so they can give way. Abraham let Lot choose the land first, and afterwards God said to him, “All the land which you see, I will give to you.” A change of mindset: giving way is not losing; in God’s hands, what we yield is what we gain.
lessons.light: 321 Light: A shift in perspective — from earthly to heavenly, from temporary to eternal. The gentle do not rely on seizing but on inheriting, because their focus is on God, not on their circumstances. Humility draws out humility and everyone wins; those who do not fight end up receiving the most.
q: Who is God? — God is the Father who gives an inheritance — how does that change the way you see gain and loss?
Who am I? — In what situation do you fight because you are afraid of losing out?
How shall I respond? — Where can you “give way” a step today?
lessons.jesus: Jesus was the heir of all things, yet on earth he had nowhere to lay his head. He did not grasp at an earthly kingdom, yet he received an everlasting one. He was obedient to the point of death, so God highly exalted him, that every knee should bow to him. “The gentle shall inherit the earth” — Jesus is the perfect proof.
lessons.pray: Father, I confess that I am often afraid of losing out and want to grab things with my own hands. Today I open my hands, trusting that my inheritance is in yours. Make me gentle — not fighting, not grabbing, not fretting — at peace to receive everything you give. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: In some small matter, freely let someone else choose first
Write down one thing you are clinging to, and pray it over into God’s hands
For one of “my 2,” give up a choice you had planned to insist on
lessons.noon: “Blessed are the gentle, for they shall inherit the earth.” — Lord, right now I let go and let you be Lord.

lessons.title: A Gentle Answer Turns Away Wrath
lessons.theme: One gentle word can put out a blaze of anger

v: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.

lessons.still: Recall the last conversation in which you raised your voice. In your mind, “replay” it: what would have happened if you had slowed down and softened? Take a deep breath and ask, “Lord, govern my mouth, and govern my heart.”
teach: An argument is like a game of table tennis: you smash the ball at me, I smash it back, and the rally gets faster and fiercer. But the moment one player stops smashing and simply catches the ball softly, the game slows down. Solomon said, “A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.”

James gives three things in order: “swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger.” We often reverse them: slow to hear, swift to speak, and swift to anger. He goes on, “the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.” We think our anger is defending what is right, but often it is only defending ourselves.

A gentle answer does not mean saying something untrue or flattering people; it means speaking the truth in a gentle tone. The content can be clear while the manner stays soft. Gentle words come from a gentle heart — everything we do flows from the heart, and when the heart is governed by the Holy Spirit, the tongue will be tamed by him too.
lessons.light: 321 Light: Pride provokes pride and both sides lose; humility draws out humility and both sides win. Arguing back from the head brings only trouble; living from the heart by the Spirit brings joy. A gentle answer is a moment of letting Jesus reign.
q: Who is God? — God is “slow to anger” — how has he responded gently to your failures?
Who am I? — With whom are you most likely to be “swift to speak and swift to anger”?
How shall I respond? — The next time there is conflict, how will you “catch the ball”?
lessons.jesus: When a Samaritan village refused to welcome Jesus, James and John wanted to call down fire from heaven to destroy it, but Jesus turned and rebuked his disciples. To the woman caught in adultery he said, “Neither do I condemn you.” His words were full of truth and full of gentleness.
lessons.pray: Lord, govern my mouth and my heart. I want to be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger. When anger rises, let the Holy Spirit remind me that the anger of man does not produce your righteousness. Make my words gentle, carrying grace and truth as yours do. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: In every conversation today, listen to the end before you speak
When you feel anger rising, lower your voice and slow down
With one of “my 2,” use gentle words to raise something you would otherwise have scolded them for
lessons.noon: “A gentle answer turns away wrath.” — Lord, right now make my words gentle.

lessons.title: Gentle with My 2
lessons.theme: Restore people with a gentle heart, and bear with them with a gentle heart

v: Brothers, even if a man is caught in some fault, you who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness, looking to yourself so that you also aren’t tempted.
with all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love,

lessons.still: Think of one of your 2 who is struggling or has fallen. Don’t judge; first pray quietly for them. Then ask yourself, “Lord, if I were in their place, how would I want to be treated?”
teach: When a doctor sets a bone, the technique must be precise and the touch must be light. Too much force causes further injury; too little, and the bone won’t go back into place. The word Paul uses for “restore” carries the sense of setting a bone or mending a fishing net. This week we have seen Jesus’ gentleness (Day 1), Moses’ humility (Day 2), the gentle inheriting the earth (Day 3), and the gentle answer (Day 4).

Paul says, “You who are spiritual must restore such a one in a spirit of gentleness.” The mark of spirituality is not pointing out faults most accurately but restoring people most gently. He adds a warning: “looking to yourself so that you also aren’t tempted.” Gentleness is rooted in humility — I know I could fall too, so I won’t look down on anyone.

Ephesians links gentleness with humility, patience and love, so that we “bear with one another.” Being gentle with my 2 means remembering that they, like me, are sinners who have received grace. Next week we will learn self-control; gentleness and self-control both belong to a life tamed by the Holy Spirit.
lessons.light: 321 Light: The practice of 920 — the “0” of the self-emptied life frees us from putting ourselves at the centre, so we can treat each of our 2 with gentleness. Life first, then relationships, then ministry; winning back a person matters more than winning an argument. People matter more than tasks; relationships matter more than things.
q: Who is God? — How has God gently restored you when you fell?
Who am I? — When others fall, are you the doctor setting the bone or the judge pronouncing the verdict?
How shall I respond? — With what kind of gentleness will you restore or bear with which of your 2?
lessons.jesus: After Peter denied him three times, the risen Jesus did not rebuke him. Instead, by the Sea of Galilee he prepared a charcoal fire and breakfast for him, and then asked him three times, “Do you love me?” Three denials were healed by three questions of love. This is what it means to restore someone in a spirit of gentleness.
lessons.pray: Lord Jesus, you once restored me gently. Make me gentle too, so that when brothers and sisters are weak I neither judge nor despise them, but humbly support them. I place my 2 in your hands; use me to be a blessing to them. In the name of the Lord Jesus we pray. Amen.
acts: Call one of “my 2” to see how they are, or send them a warm message
Pray for someone who is going through a weak time, and ask them what help they need
Tomorrow (Saturday), share this week’s practice of gentleness with your spiritual companion
lessons.noon: “With all lowliness and humility, with patience, bearing with one another in love” — Lord, right now let me treat people with gentleness.
